parent_r8b1.observation: PHP h=4 is width-4 resolution refutable, although k=4 exact elimination alone hits a width barrier; therefore R8B1 did not kill the fixed-width-4 resolution tooth.

mission: Continue the hostile hunt with a preexisting bounded-degree high-treewidth Tseitin family and ask whether known proof-complexity theorems force resolution width to grow beyond every fixed constant, in particular beyond 4.

existing_family.underlying_graph: two copies of an m x m toroidal grid, m=8R+13

external_theorem_dependencies.source: ECCC TR19-178 / de Colnet-Mengel related proof-complexity literature
external_theorem_dependencies.statement: For bounded-degree Tseitin formulas, minimum resolution width is Theta(treewidth of the underlying graph), as summarized in the cited proof-complexity literature.
An m x m grid has treewidth m; the m x m toroidal grid contains an m x m grid subgraph, hence its treewidth grows at least linearly in m.

barrier_logic: Since degree is constant and tw(G_R) grows unboundedly with m=8R+13, w(T(G_R,c)) also grows unboundedly. Therefore there exists R0 such that for all sufficiently large R, the UNSAT toroidal Tseitin member requires resolution width >4. This is an asymptotic family barrier, not a claim about the smallest concrete R.
claim_boundary: If the theorem audit passes, fixed k=4 resolution is falsified as a universal standalone resolution tooth. This does not falsify the full multi-rule TRUMP architecture, because a different exact polynomial structural rule (for example parity/XOR reasoning) could solve Tseitin formulas. It does not prove P!=NP.
